note: He plausibly meets 'successful' — runs his own business, sells for a living, and is taking a three-month family trip through Europe — and health is unambiguously the neglected corner of an otherwise functioning life, which is the criterion he fits best. He misses everything else. Income fails outright and by his own disclosure: zero liquid cash, available funds already committed to credit-card bills for flights, and a stated ceiling far below the price. Good-to-great fails completely: he has never exercised in his life and has never played a sport, so this is a from-zero build, not an optimisation. The exclusion criterion is the interesting one — he is lean rather than 50 lb overweight, so he passes on the body half, but he fails on the attitude half the ICP quote actually names, since he would rather watch television than train and finds gyms pointless. Read against the criteria as written rather than against the outcome, this prospect should not have reached a closer, and the rep's own disqualification at the end was the correct call arriving about forty minutes late.
